title: Splitting Code: Prototypes and Headers
instructions: Real programs are split across many files. To let one file use a function defined elsewhere, you give C a PROTOTYPE first.
A prototype is just the function's name and shape, with a semicolon and no body: int square(int n);
It tells C 'this function exists, trust me, the body is somewhere.' Then you can define the body later, even below main.
In big projects, these prototypes are collected into a header file (ending in .h) that other files #include. The bodies live in matching .c files.
Here we do it all in one file so it runs in this window: a prototype at the top, the body at the bottom.
task: Finish the square function's body so it prints:  square(5) = 25
hint:
